purpose: Cefoxitin is an antibiotic used to treat or prevent serious bacterial infections. It can be used for infections in the abdomen, pelvis, skin, lungs, urinary tract, and bones. It is also given before certain surgeries to help prevent infection from developing.
how_it_works: Cefoxitin works by attacking the outer wall that surrounds bacteria. Without a strong wall, the bacteria fall apart and die. Your body's immune system can then clean up the remaining bacteria, helping you recover from the infection.
common_side_effects: Some common side effects include pain, redness, or swelling at the injection site, nausea, diarrhea, rash, or a mild fever. You may also notice your veins feeling sore if it is given through an IV. Most of these side effects are mild and go away on their own.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are allergic to penicillin or any other antibiotics, as you may also be allergic to cefoxitin. Contact your doctor right away if you develop a severe rash, difficulty breathing, or watery or bloody diarrhea, as these can be signs of a serious reaction. Let your healthcare team know about all medications you take, especially blood thinners, since cefoxitin can interact with some drugs.
typical_dosing: Cefoxitin is given as an injection or through an IV by a healthcare provider — you will not take this medication at home as a pill. For most infections, it is given every 6 to 8 hours, but your doctor will decide the right dose and schedule based on your specific infection and how well your kidneys are working.
